summary: Grasshopper Manufacture's Suda51-created hack-and-slash series starring Travis Touchdown, including mainline entries, Travis Strikes Again, and the Japan-only mobile spin-off.

entries.title: No More Heroes
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC port for original-version fidelity; PS3 Heroes' Paradise for added HD-port content

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or RPCS3/Dolphin for comparison
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main run; use PS3 emulation or hardware for Heroes' Paradise additions if needed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC port, with PS3 Heroes' Paradise as a content supplement

primary.version: 2021 PC port of the original version
primary.why: The original Wii game later received an enhanced Heroes' Paradise HD port on PS3/Xbox 360 with additional content, then a modern port of the original version on Switch, Amazon Luna, and Windows. Windows is the clean high-fidelity route for the original version, while PS3 Heroes' Paradise is worth a secondary check for its added content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 2021 Windows version natively for the main run; then play the PS3 Heroes' Paradise content if you want the HD port's additional material.

secondary.exclusive_content: No More Heroes: Heroes' Paradise additional content and PlayStation Move support
secondary.what_to_play: Check the Heroes' Paradise additions after the Windows main run.
secondary.why: Heroes' Paradise is documented as an enhanced port with additional content, but the Windows release is the modern high-fidelity route for the original version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Heroes' Paradise is an enhanced port with added content, but criticism of missing original-version details and the split between localized PS3 and Japan-only Xbox 360 makes it a secondary route rather than the default main run.

entries.title: No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or Dolphin for original Wii
emulation.notes: Use Windows for play; Dolphin only for original control/presentation comparison.

primary.why: No More Heroes 2 originally released on Wii, then came to Nintendo Switch, Amazon Luna, and Windows. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route for the sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 2021 Windows version natively; use Switch as a portable alternative if preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: Modern ports preserve the game outside Wii hardware; no cited separate enhanced-content edition exists.

entries.title: No More Heroes: World Ranker
entries.definitive_edition: No active definitive edition; Android/iOS archival documentation only

emulation.emulator: No stable live-service emulation route documented
emulation.notes: Treat as an unavailable mobile live-service spin-off unless a preserved legal build/server path is found.

primary.why: World Ranker was a Japan-only Android and iOS social/mobile spin-off. It has since been removed from servers, so Android is only an archival documentation route rather than a normal playable recommendation.
primary.how_to_play: No normal live-service route is currently documented; preserve through screenshots, footage, and any legally retained device/build access rather than planning a fresh playthrough.

entries.remaster_caveats: Server removal means this entry is documented for completeness but is not normally playable today.

entries.title: Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes

emulation.notes: Use the PC Complete Edition natively.

primary.why: Travis Strikes Again launched on Nintendo Switch in January 2019 and came to PlayStation 4 and Windows later in 2019 as Complete Edition. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Complete Edition natively; use PS4 as a console alternative or Switch for the original portable release.

entries.remaster_caveats: The later PS4/Windows versions are Complete Edition ports of the Switch original.

entries.title: No More Heroes III

emulation.notes: Use the Windows enhanced version natively.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC enhanced version; PS5/Xbox Series X/S provide 4K/60fps console routes

primary.why: No More Heroes III launched on Switch in 2021, then received enhanced PlayStation, Xbox, and Windows versions in 2022 with improved visuals and performance. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route, while PS5/Xbox Series X/S are excellent 4K/60fps console alternatives.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively at the highest stable settings; use PS5 or Xbox Series X/S if you want a console 4K/60fps route.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch original is the first release, but the later versions improve visuals and performance.
